title: sync's scan, its attachment test and attachment_path_fault spell intent/ whatever intent_dir says, and the attachment test is a second owner-of-a-path answer
body:
## What happens

A project's intent directory is configurable (`intent_dir` in `intent/.config/config.json`, read by `Project::intent_dir`). `Fixture::with_intent_dir` exists so that a site spelling `intent/` itself is caught. Several sites still spell it, because they hold no `Project`:

- `sync.rs`: `Scanned::includes` (`self.root.join("intent")`, about :619) and `candidates` (`root.join("intent")`, about :813) root the whole sync corpus at `intent/`. `organize::observe` reads the tree through `sync::scan`, so organize inherits it.
- `sync.rs`'s `is_carried_attachment` strips `intent/st/` and `intent/.canon/st/` (about :1251). It is a second answer to which thread owns a path, beside `Project::owner_of` (ST0095 WP-14). It stays because `scan(root, previous)` has no `Project` to ask.
- `project.rs`'s `attachment_path_fault` tests `rel.starts_with("intent/st")` (about :191), and `PathFault::why` names `intent/st/<ID>` in its messages (about :108 and :200).
- `intentd`'s `watch.rs` builds `root.join("intent")` (about :189).

For a project with any other `intent_dir`, sync scans a directory that does not exist, and organize sees nothing. The attachment door's repo-relative check then misses the repository-relative spelling it exists to catch.

## The fix

Give `sync::scan` (and the watch) the project's intent directory from the one `Project`. Make `is_carried_attachment` ask `Project::owner_of`, and give `attachment_path_fault` the project's `st_dir`. With that, no site spells `intent/` but `Project` and the config default. Prove it with `Fixture::with_intent_dir`.

Found by dc's census for ST0095 WP-14 (2026-11-20), which converted every owner-of-a-path answer that holds a `Project`. Not caused by WP-14. It rides this release (hv decision 69), and vc sequences it.
